title: Lending and finance compliance
summary: The licences behind finance offers, honest cost disclosure, predatory lending red flags, platform rules for credit ads and consent-first data handling. You finish able to vet a lender, show the true cost, collect data lawfully and pull traffic fast when a partner changes. Education, not legal advice.

lessons.title: Licences: the lender's, the intermediary's and yours
objectives: By the end you can tell which licence the product needs and which one the seller needs.
You can check whether you, as the marketer, might need authorisation yourself.
You can verify a lender or insurer's legal entity on an official register.
You can apply a written licence rule before every launch.

steps.h: Why one missing licence voids everything
steps.p: If the lender is not licensed for your geo, every lead you send helps an illegal business, payouts can be withheld, and your ad account carries the risk. In some markets, the person who brings customers to a lender needs permission too. Licence checks come before creatives.
steps.more: The general compliance module covered how law, licences, platform policy and network rules stack. This lesson goes one level deeper for finance: there are usually three different permissions in play, and many affiliates check only the first. A lender can be licensed while the comparison site that sends it leads is not, and in some countries that site is doing a regulated activity. Treat this lesson as education, not legal advice.

d.s: Check the product, the seller and yourself.

steps.say: If the lender isn't licensed for your geo, every lead you send helps an illegal business. Payouts can be withheld, and your ad account carries the risk. In some markets, the person who brings customers to a lender needs permission too. So licence checks come before creatives. No licence, no launch. Check the product, the seller, and yourself. And remember, this lesson is education, not legal advice.

steps.h: Three permissions to think about
steps.p: Each one answers a different question. You need a clear answer to all three for each geo before spending, and the answer can differ from one country to the next.
steps.more: In the UK, for example, credit broking, which includes introducing people to lenders, is a regulated activity that needs FCA authorisation at the time of writing, and lead generators have been a focus of the FCA. In parts of the US, loan brokers and lead generators may need state licences. Insurance in most countries can only be sold through licensed insurers, brokers or agents, and introducing customers can count as intermediation. We are not certain how each African market treats affiliates who only run ads; ask a local adviser.
d: The product's provider|Is the lender, insurer or bank licensed to offer this here?
The intermediary|Does the broker, aggregator or network need its own permission?
You|Does bringing customers count as a regulated activity where you run?
steps.say: There are three permissions to think about, and each answers a different question. Look at the cards. The product's provider: is the lender, insurer or bank licensed to offer this here? The intermediary: does the broker, aggregator or network need its own permission? And you: does bringing customers count as a regulated activity where you run? You need a clear answer to all three, for each geo, before spending. We're not certain how each African market treats affiliates who only run ads, so ask a local adviser.

steps.h: Who licenses what: examples to verify
steps.p: Examples at the time of writing. Bodies, names and powers change, and some areas are under reform. Always confirm on the official site and search the legal entity name, not the brand.
steps.more: Nigeria's FCCPC issued dedicated rules for digital and non-traditional consumer lenders, most recently in 2025 at the time of writing; check whether they cover agents or marketers. Kenya has required non-deposit-taking digital credit providers to be licensed by the Central Bank since 2022. South Africa's National Credit Act requires credit providers to register above set thresholds and sets maximum rates. Cameroon is part of the CEMAC banking regime and the CIMA insurance code; local rules also apply. We are not certain this is current; check the regulator's official site and a local adviser before relying on it.
steps.say: Here are examples of who licenses what, at the time of writing. Read the table. In Nigeria, lending sits with the C B N, with the F C C P C for digital lenders, and insurance with NAICOM. In Kenya, the Central Bank of Kenya and the Insurance Regulatory Authority. In Ghana, the Bank of Ghana and the National Insurance Commission. South Africa, the National Credit Regulator, and the F S C A with the Prudential Authority. Cameroon's regional bodies need checking. And the U K, the F C A. Bodies and powers change, so always confirm on the official site, and search the legal entity name, not the brand.

steps.h: Verify the legal entity, step by step
steps.p: Do this for every lender, insurer or bank you promote, in every geo. It takes about 15 minutes. Screens are illustrative mock-ups, not real registers.

steps.title: Get the legal entity name
steps.text: Ask the network for the exact company name and licence number for this geo. A brand name is not enough.

messages.text: Which legal entity lends to Kenyan users on this offer, and what is its licence number?
Example Credit Ltd, CBK digital credit licence. Number in the attached letter.

steps.title: Open the official register
steps.text: Type the regulator's address yourself. Never use a link from the offer page or the lender's site.

steps.title: Match name, type and status
steps.text: The entity must match exactly, the licence type must cover this product, and the status must be active.

steps.title: Match the app and the terms
steps.text: The app store developer name and the loan terms must show the same legal entity. A different name is a red flag.

steps.title: Check warnings and file it
steps.text: Search the regulator's warning list and news for the brand. Screenshot every page with the date into your offer folder.

steps.say: Do this for every lender, insurer or bank you promote, in every geo. It takes about fifteen minutes. Step one: ask the network for the exact legal entity name and licence number. A brand isn't enough. Step two: open the official register by typing the regulator's address yourself, never from a link on the offer page. Step three: match the name, licence type and active status. Step four: check the app store developer name and loan terms show the same entity. Step five: search the warning list and news, and screenshot everything with the date into your offer folder.

steps.h: Licence twists in cards, insurance and banking
steps.p: Lending is not the only product with a licence behind it. Each of these has a common trap where the brand you see is not the licensed party, so check who actually provides the product.
steps.more: Many finance apps in our core markets are technology companies that partner with a licensed bank, microfinance bank or insurer. That can be fine, but the claims in your ad must match the licensed partner's product, and statements such as 'your money is protected' are only true if a licensed institution covered by a protection scheme holds the deposits. We are not certain this is current; check the regulator's official site and a local adviser before relying on it.
d: Fintech apps|Often run on a partner bank's licence; check the bank
Insurance|Insurer carries risk; broker or agent sells it
BNPL|Rules vary; consumer law still applies
Savings apps|Deposit protection only if a licensed bank holds it
steps.say: Lending isn't the only product with a licence behind it. Each of these has a trap where the brand you see isn't the licensed party. Look at the cards. Fintech apps often run on a partner bank's licence, so check the bank. With insurance, the insurer carries the risk while a broker or agent sells it. B N P L, buy now pay later, rules vary, but consumer law still applies. And savings apps only have deposit protection if a licensed bank holds the money. Your ad's claims must match the licensed partner's product.

steps.h: The licence type must match the product
steps.p: A licence covers specific activities. A real licence for the wrong activity is not enough. Rough guide; categories and names differ by country, so read what each licence actually permits.
steps.say: A licence covers specific activities, so a real licence for the wrong activity isn't enough. Read the table. A digital credit provider usually covers lending, but not taking deposits. A microfinance bank covers small loans and deposits, but not activity beyond its tier. A payment service provider covers payments and wallets, but not lending. An insurance broker arranges cover but doesn't carry the risk. An insurer underwrites policies but doesn't do banking. Categories differ by country, so read what each licence actually permits.

steps.h: Brand versus legal entity
steps.p: Many problems hide in the gap between the name on the ad and the company that signs the contract. Check the second, because that is the one the regulator licensed.

Check the entity, because that's the one the regulator licensed.

steps.h: Worked example: what an unlicensed lender costs you
steps.p: Example, illustrative. You run a loan offer for 30 days, then the lender turns out to be unlicensed for your geo. The network voids the month, and the account takes a hit as well.
steps.more: Check: you were heading for $3,200 - $2,400 = $800 profit. Instead you paid $2,400 for nothing. The 15-minute check would have stopped it. Network terms commonly allow withholding payouts for traffic to offers that break law or terms; read yours.
steps.say: Here's an illustrative example of what an unlicensed lender costs you. You run a loan offer for thirty days, spending two thousand four hundred dollars. You earn three thousand two hundred in payouts, but then the lender turns out to be unlicensed for your geo, and the network voids the month. Paid to you: zero. Net result: minus two thousand four hundred dollars, plus account restriction risk. You were heading for eight hundred dollars profit. The fifteen minute check would have stopped it.

steps.h: When the network cannot answer
steps.p: A vague reply about licences is an answer in itself. Ask once, politely and in writing, then wait for a clear answer before spending. Chat is illustrative.

lessons.title: Cost disclosure: APR, total cost and representative examples
objectives: By the end you can explain interest rate, APR, fees and total repayable in plain words.
You can see why a flat monthly rate understates the real yearly cost.
You can present a loan's cost honestly in an ad and on a page.
You can apply exact rules for where cost information sits.

steps.h: Why the cost is the most important line
steps.p: A borrower's main question is what the loan will cost them. Hiding or shrinking that answer is how people end up in debt they did not expect, and it is the claim regulators check first. Clear cost also brings better leads: people who apply knowing the price are more likely to go ahead.

d.b: Show the cost before the click
d.s: Clear cost protects the borrower, your account and your approval rate.

steps.say: A borrower's main question is what the loan will cost them. Hiding or shrinking that answer is how people end up in debt they didn't expect, and it's the claim regulators check first. Clear cost also brings better leads, because people who apply knowing the price are more likely to go ahead. So show the cost before the click. It protects the borrower, your account and your approval rate.

steps.h: Cost words, in plain English
steps.p: Learn these five terms so you can read a lender's terms and spot when an ad uses the wrong one. Exact legal definitions differ by country.
d: Interest rate|Price of borrowing, as a percentage, often per month or per year
Fees|Set charges: processing, service, late, insurance add-ons
APR|Yearly cost including interest and required fees, per local formula
Total repayable|Everything the borrower pays back, in money
Representative example|A typical loan with its full cost, set out in one place
steps.say: Learn these five terms. Look at the cards. Interest rate: the price of borrowing as a percentage, often per month or per year. Fees: set charges like processing, service, late fees and insurance add-ons. A P R, annual percentage rate: the yearly cost including interest and required fees, using the local formula. Total repayable: everything the borrower pays back, in money. And a representative example: a typical loan with its full cost in one place. Exact legal definitions differ by country.

steps.h: Worked example: a flat monthly rate
steps.p: Example. Borrow 100,000 for 12 months at '3% a month flat'. Flat means interest is charged on the full amount every month, even as it is repaid. It sounds like 36% a year. It is not.
steps.more: Example maths. Interest: 100,000 x 0.03 x 12 = 36,000. Total repayable 136,000, or about 11,333 a month. Because the borrower pays the balance down every month but is still charged on the full 100,000, the real rate on the money they actually hold is about 5.1% a month. That is roughly 61% a year as a simple rate, and about 81% once monthly compounding is counted. The official APR uses a formula set by each country. Never calculate the APR yourself for an ad; get it from the lender.
d: 36,000 interest
Total repayable:
steps.say: Here's a worked example. Borrow one hundred thousand for twelve months at three percent a month, flat. Flat means interest is charged on the full amount every month, even as it's repaid. Look at the equation: one hundred thousand times three percent times twelve is thirty six thousand interest, so the total repayable is one hundred and thirty six thousand. It sounds like thirty six percent a year. It isn't. Because the balance falls but interest doesn't, the real cost is much higher. Never calculate the A P R yourself for an ad; get it from the lender.

steps.h: The same loan, three ways to present it
steps.p: Example, from the loan above. All three lines are arithmetic facts. Only one gives a borrower a fair picture without extra work. Lenders and regulators decide the required form; this shows why it matters.

rows: 'Borrow 100,000, repay 136,000 over 12 months. APR as stated by lender'

steps.say: Here's the same loan, presented three ways. Read the table. Only three percent a month makes the reader think about thirty six percent a year, cheap. Pay eleven thousand three hundred and thirty three a month sounds affordable, but the cost is unclear. Borrow one hundred thousand, repay one hundred and thirty six thousand over twelve months, with the A P R as stated by the lender, gives a clear total cost. All three are arithmetic facts, but only one gives a fair picture without extra work.

steps.h: Worked example: fees taken upfront
steps.p: Example. A 14-day loan advertised as 20,000. A 20% processing fee is deducted, so the borrower receives 16,000 but repays 24,000. The cost is 8,000 on 16,000 received.
steps.more: Check: 20,000 x 20% = 4,000 deducted, so 16,000 received. Repay 24,000. Cost = 24,000 - 16,000 = 8,000. 8,000 / 16,000 = 50% for 14 days. Simple annualised: 50% x 365 / 14 = about 1,304%. An ad saying 'get 20,000' hides that the borrower only gets 16,000. Upfront deductions like this are a common complaint against digital lenders and a predatory red flag covered in the next lesson.

/ 16,000 received
50% in 14 days
about 1,300% a year (simple)
steps.say: Another worked example: fees taken upfront. A fourteen day loan is advertised as twenty thousand. A twenty percent processing fee is deducted, so the borrower receives sixteen thousand, but repays twenty four thousand. Look at the equation. The cost is eight thousand on sixteen thousand received. That's fifty percent in fourteen days, or about one thousand three hundred percent a year as a simple rate. An ad saying get twenty thousand hides that the borrower only gets sixteen.

steps.h: Mentioning a cost often means showing all of it
steps.p: In several places, once an ad mentions a rate, a payment or a fee, it must also show fuller cost information, such as an APR and a representative example. Partial numbers that make a loan look cheap are what these rules target.
steps.more: Examples at the time of writing: in the US, certain terms in a credit ad, such as a payment amount or number of payments, trigger extra disclosures under federal rules. In the UK, consumer credit rules say when a representative APR and representative example are required, and the representative APR must be one that a set share of borrowers are expected to get, so 'from 9.9%' for a rate few receive is not allowed. We are not certain of the equivalent triggers in Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa or Cameroon. Ask the lender for the required wording per geo and use it exactly.

d.b: One cost figure can trigger full disclosure
d.s: If you mention a number, expect to show the full cost.

steps.h: A disclosure block you can reuse
steps.p: Keep the disclosure as one block you paste into every ad variant and page, filled with the lender's figures. Editing it per ad is where errors creep in.

steps.say: Keep the disclosure as one reusable block. On screen is a template. I won't read the placeholders, but notice it covers the amount and term, the monthly repayment, the total repayable, the A P R and rate type, the fees, the lender's legal entity and regulator, and a line that approval isn't guaranteed. Paste it into every ad and page, filled with the lender's figures. Editing it per ad is where errors creep in. Use the exact wording your lender and regulator require for each geo.

steps.h: Rewrite: hidden cost versus clear cost
steps.p: Same loan, same audience. The left version gets more clicks from people who will be shocked later. The right version gets fewer, better-informed applicants who are more likely to be approved and to go ahead.
steps.say: Same loan, same audience. Compare the columns. The hidden cost version says get twenty thousand in five minutes, low monthly rate, everyone qualifies, with fees in tiny grey text. It gets more clicks from people who'll be shocked later. The clear cost version says borrow twenty thousand, receive sixteen thousand after the fee, total repayable twenty four thousand in fourteen days, approval depends on checks, with the cost above the button. Fewer clicks, but better-informed applicants who are more likely to be approved.

steps.h: Never round down or leave out costs
steps.p: A disclosure that is accurate but hidden can still mislead. A disclosure that is visible but wrong is worse, because people rely on it when they decide to borrow.

d.text: Use the lender's official APR and representative example, never your own calculation. Show them where people look, not in footers. Never omit mandatory fees, insurance add-ons or upfront deductions. We are not certain this is current; check the regulator's official site and a local adviser before relying on it.

steps.h: Common disclosure mistakes
steps.p: Each of these turns an approved ad into a misleading one. Most happen when a buyer shortens text to fit a creative or copies a competitor's ad.
d: Monthly rate shown alone|Add total repayable and APR
'From' rates few people get|Use the representative figure
Old figures after a price change|Date and recheck every 30 days
Disclosure cut on mobile|Check every placement preview
steps.say: Each of these mistakes turns an approved ad into a misleading one, usually when a buyer shortens text to fit a creative or copies a competitor. Look at the cards. A monthly rate shown alone, so add total repayable and A P R. From rates that few people get, so use the representative figure. Old figures after a price change, so date and recheck every thirty days. And a disclosure cut on mobile, so check every placement preview.

steps.h: Why this lesson exists
steps.p: Some lenders make money mainly when borrowers fail: hidden fees, rollovers, penalties and shaming collection. Affiliates who send them traffic share in that harm. Regulators in our core markets have acted against digital lenders for these practices, and platforms remove their ads.
steps.more: Predatory lending is not the same as expensive lending. A short loan can be costly and still be honest if the cost is clear, the lender checks affordability and treats borrowers fairly. It becomes predatory when the design relies on people not understanding the cost, not being able to repay, or being pressured into paying through fear and shame. In Nigeria and Kenya, regulators have acted against digital lenders over debt shaming and misuse of phone contacts, and Kenya's data protection regulator has fined lenders over this at the time of writing. We are not certain this is current; check the regulator's official site and a local adviser before relying on it.

d.s: If the business needs borrowers to struggle, do not feed it.

steps.h: Red flags in the lender
steps.p: One flag is enough to stop and investigate. Two or more and you refuse the offer. These are signs, not legal tests; when in doubt, do not run it.

Cost hidden until after applying|No total repayable upfront
Fees taken from the loan|Borrower receives far less
Very short terms with rollovers|Debt grows, never shrinks
Contact or gallery access|Used for shaming collection
No affordability check|Approves people who cannot repay
steps.say: Here are the red flags in a lender. One flag is enough to stop and investigate. Two or more, and you refuse. Look at the cards. Not on the register, or the entity doesn't match. Cost hidden until after applying. Fees taken from the loan, so the borrower receives far less. Very short terms with rollovers, so debt grows and never shrinks. Contact or gallery access, used for shaming collection. And no affordability check. These are signs, not legal tests. When in doubt, don't run it.

steps.h: Harm to the borrower, in numbers
steps.p: Example, illustrative figures. Each practice turns a small loan into a much bigger burden. When you see these in terms or reviews, picture the person on the other end.
steps.more: Check: 1,500 x 4 = 6,000. A 1% daily late fee on a 10,000 balance for 30 days, charged on the original balance, adds 3,000, which is 30%. Some countries cap fees, late charges or the total that can be collected; others do not. Your job is not to calculate the legal limit, it is to refuse offers where the business model depends on charges like these.
steps.say: Here's the harm in numbers, with illustrative figures. Read the table. An upfront fee of twenty percent on a twenty thousand loan means receiving sixteen thousand, but repaying twenty four. Rollovers, a one thousand five hundred fee over four periods, means six thousand paid, with ten thousand still owed. A daily late fee of one percent for thirty days adds thirty percent to the balance. And bundled add-on insurance is an extra cost nobody asked for. When you see these in terms or reviews, picture the person on the other end.

steps.h: Spot an advance-fee loan scam
steps.p: A common scam: a 'lender' approves anyone, then asks for an upfront fee to release the loan. No loan ever arrives. Never promote or forward anything like this. Chat is an illustrative example of a scam.
steps.more: Signs: guaranteed approval, an upfront fee to a personal account, pressure with a deadline, and contact through chat apps. Licensed lenders deduct fees in the loan terms or charge them with repayments; they do not demand payment to release funds. If someone presents this as an affiliate offer, it is fraud. Report it to the network and do not run it.

messages.text: Congratulations, your 200,000 loan is APPROVED. No credit check.
To release it, pay a 10,000 activation fee to this account today.
Why can't the fee come out of the loan?
System rules. Offer expires in 1 hour.

steps.say: Here's a common scam, the advance-fee loan. Read the chat. A so-called lender says your two hundred thousand loan is approved, no credit check. Then it asks for a ten thousand activation fee to release it, today. When asked why the fee can't come out of the loan, it says system rules, and the offer expires in one hour. No loan ever arrives. Licensed lenders don't demand payment to release funds. Never promote or forward anything like this, and report it to the network.

steps.h: Targeting need versus targeting desperation
steps.p: You can make a predatory outcome more likely with your own creative choices, even on a licensed offer. The angle decides who clicks, and the people who click decide what happens next.

a.title: Desperation angles (refuse)
items: Can't pay rent? We approve anyone

b.title: Need angles (honest)
items: Spread the cost of a planned purchase

Desperation angles, which you refuse: broke, get cash in five minutes, can't pay rent, bad credit no questions, and images of bills and eviction. Need angles, which are honest: spread the cost of a planned purchase, check eligibility before you apply, see the full cost upfront, and calm, factual imagery. The angle decides who clicks, and who clicks decides what happens next.

steps.p: This is a firm line in this school. It protects people from debt traps, and it protects your ad accounts, your network relationships and your name.

steps.h: Why platform rules for credit exist
steps.p: Credit ads were used to exclude people by age, gender or postcode, so platforms limit how they can be targeted. Platforms also restrict high-cost and short-term lending. Breaking these rules gets ads rejected and accounts restricted, often with little warning.

d.b: Credit ads play by stricter rules
d.s: Less targeting, more disclosure, more review.

steps.say: Credit ads were once used to exclude people by age, gender or postcode, so platforms now limit how they can be targeted. Platforms also restrict high-cost and short-term lending. steps.h: Declaring a special ad category
steps.p: On Meta, credit ads must be declared in a special ad category in many regions. Category names have changed and coverage differs by country. We are not certain of the current names or which African markets require it; check Meta's Help Center and Ads Manager.

In some regions it has broadened the credit category into a wider financial products and services category. Where a category applies, targeting options are reduced. We are not certain which countries in Africa currently require it or exactly what it limits there. Read the policy page for each country before you launch, and save a dated screenshot to your file.

steps.h: Words and angles reviewers flag in finance ads
steps.p: At the time of writing, Meta's personal attributes rules say ads must not assert or imply things about the viewer, and vulnerable financial status is on that list. Approval claims are also a common rejection reason. Check the current policy wording.

steps.h: Why data is the product in finance lead gen
steps.p: In lead generation you are not selling a click, you are passing a person's financial details to a company. That makes you responsible for how the data was collected, who it goes to and how long it is kept. Data protection law in our core markets applies to you.

d.b: You are handling people's financial lives
d.s: Consent and care are part of the product.

steps.say: In lead generation, you're not selling a click. You're passing a person's financial details to a company. That makes you responsible for how the data was collected, who it goes to, and how long it's kept. Data protection law in our core markets applies to you. You're handling people's financial lives, so consent and care are part of the product.

steps.h: Four tests of valid consent
steps.p: Most modern data laws use similar ideas. Exact wording differs, so read your country's guidance, but if your consent fails one of these, it probably fails the law too.
d: Freely given|Not a condition for something unrelated
Specific|Separate for each purpose: matching, marketing, sharing
Informed|Says who gets the data and why, in plain words
Clear action|A tick or tap, never a pre-ticked box
steps.say: Most modern data laws use similar ideas, shown on these four cards. Freely given: not a condition for something unrelated. Specific: separate for each purpose, like matching, marketing and sharing. Informed: it says who gets the data and why, in plain words. And a clear action: a tick or tap, never a pre-ticked box. Exact wording differs, so read your country's guidance. But if your consent fails one of these tests, it probably fails the law too.

steps.h: Data protection laws in core markets
steps.p: Examples at the time of writing. Several of these regulators require controllers to register, and rules on transfers abroad apply. We are not certain this is current; check the regulator's official site and a local adviser before relying on it.
steps.more: Kenya and Ghana require many data controllers and processors to register with the regulator, and Nigeria's NDPC has registration duties for major controllers at the time of writing. South Africa's POPIA has specific rules on direct marketing by electronic means. In the US, rules on consent for marketing calls and texts (TCPA) have changed and been disputed in court recently; we are not certain of the current position, so get US-specific legal advice before running US finance lead gen.
steps.say: Here are the data protection laws in our core markets, at the time of writing. Read the table. Nigeria has the Nigeria Data Protection Act twenty twenty three, with the N D P C. steps.h: Bundled consent versus clear consent
steps.p: Bundled consent hides sharing inside terms nobody reads. It usually fails the law, and networks and lenders may reject leads that rely on it. Clear consent costs some volume and keeps the rest.

a.title: Bundled (avoid)
items: 'By submitting you agree to our terms'
Partners listed only on another page

b.title: Clear (use)
items: Separate tick to share with named lenders
Partner list linked next to the tick

steps.say: Compare these two approaches. Bundled consent, which you avoid: by submitting you agree to our terms, partners listed only on another page, a pre-ticked marketing box, and one tick for everything. Clear consent, which you use: a separate tick to share with named lenders, a partner list linked next to the tick, unticked boxes the user chooses, and matching, marketing and sharing separated. Bundled consent usually fails the law, and lenders may reject those leads. Clear consent costs some volume and keeps the rest.

steps.p: Each purpose has its own control, the recipients are named or linked, and the privacy policy is one tap away. Screen is an illustrative mock-up.

steps.h: Worked example: only consented leads are billable
steps.p: Example. 1,000 people submit the form. 720 tick the sharing box. Only those 720 may be passed to lenders. Plan revenue on 720, never on 1,000.
steps.more: Check: 720 x 88% valid = about 634. 634 x 24% approved = about 152. At $25 per approval that is $3,800, or $3.80 per submit. A buyer who planned on all 1,000 submits being sold would expect over $5,000 and might be tempted to pass on people who did not tick. That is a breach, and it is the most common data mistake in this vertical.

steps.p: For every lead, store enough to prove who agreed to what, when and on which version of the wording. Keep it as long as you keep the lead.

steps.h: Handling a deletion request
steps.p: People can ask what you hold and ask you to delete it. Have one simple process and follow it every time. Screens are illustrative mock-ups.

steps.title: Receive and log
steps.text: Log the request with the date. Many laws set deadlines measured in days or weeks; check yours.

Thank you. We have logged your request today and will confirm when it is done.

steps.text: Search the form tool, tracker, sheets and any partner you sent it to.

steps.title: Delete and tell partners
steps.text: Delete your copies and tell each partner who received the lead, in writing.

steps.title: Confirm and keep a note
steps.text: Confirm to the person. Keep only a minimal note that the request was handled, as your adviser recommends.

steps.say: People can ask what you hold and ask you to delete it, so have one simple process. Step one: receive and log the request with the date, because many laws set deadlines in days or weeks. steps.p: Lead lists are the fastest way to break data law in this vertical. They also usually perform badly, because the people on them never asked to hear from you.

steps.p: Each of these is easy to make when moving fast. Each one can lead to a complaint to a regulator, a fine or the network rejecting all your leads.

Leads stored in personal chats|Use one controlled system
Sent to partners not shown|Show the current partner list

lessons.title: After launch: monitoring partners and pulling traffic
objectives: By the end you can run a monthly compliance check on live finance offers.
You can test your own funnel as a user would see it.
You can rank incidents by severity and act within set times.
You can pull traffic calmly and in writing when a partner changes.

steps.h: Why compliance does not end at launch
steps.p: Lenders change fees, apps change permissions, licences get suspended, and networks swap advertisers behind the same offer link. A campaign that was clean at launch can be harmful a month later without you changing anything.

d.b: Clean at launch is not clean forever
d.s: Partners change. Your checks must repeat.

steps.say: Lenders change fees, apps change permissions, licences get suspended, and networks swap advertisers behind the same offer link. So a campaign that was clean at launch can be harmful a month later, without you changing anything. Clean at launch isn't clean forever. Partners change, so your checks must repeat.

steps.h: Monthly monitoring routine
steps.p: Put this on a fixed date each month for every live finance offer. It takes about 30 minutes per offer and catches most problems before a regulator, platform or network does.
d: Recheck register and warning list
Walk your own funnel
Read new low-star reviews
Compare terms with your file
Review complaints and scrubs
Record the outcome
steps.say: Here's a monthly monitoring routine. Put it on a fixed date for every live finance offer. Follow the steps: recheck the register and warning list, walk your own funnel, read new low-star reviews, compare the terms with your file, review complaints and scrubs, and record the outcome. It takes about thirty minutes per offer, and catches most problems before a regulator, platform or network does.

steps.h: Incident severity and response time
steps.p: Starting rules to adapt. Decide in advance how fast you act on each kind of problem, so nobody debates while harm continues. Share the table with anyone on your team who runs finance offers.

rows: Lender licence suspended or not found
Redirect goes to a different lender
Upfront fee or shaming reports appear

steps.say: Decide in advance how fast you act on each problem, so nobody debates while harm continues. Read the table. A lender licence suspended or not found, a redirect to a different lender, or upfront fee or shaming reports: all critical, so pause now. Fees or terms changed, or a disclosure cut in a placement: high, so act within twenty four hours. A complaint rate up two times: medium, within three days. These are starting rules to adapt, so share them with your team.

steps.h: Worked example: pausing early is cheaper
steps.p: Example. A lender's licence is suspended. Pausing the same day costs one day's profit. Waiting for the monthly check risks voided payouts and an account review.
steps.more: Example figures. If you earn $100 a day in payouts and $80 a day profit, 20 more days at risk is $2,000 of payouts a network may void, plus the spend. The pause costs $80 of profit. Fast action is almost always the cheaper choice in regulated verticals.

vs wait 20 days:
$2,000 payouts at risk
steps.say: Here's a worked example of why pausing early is cheaper. A lender's licence is suspended. Look at the equation. If you pause today, you lose one day's profit, eighty dollars. If you wait twenty days for the monthly check, you have two thousand dollars of payouts at risk that a network may void, plus the spend. Fast action is almost always the cheaper choice in regulated verticals. These are example figures.

steps.h: Pulling traffic in writing
steps.p: Pause first, then tell the network in writing what you found and what you need before resuming. Keep it factual and specific, with dates and screenshots. Chat is illustrative.

messages.text: I paused the KE loan offer today. The fee on the live page is 15%, my file shows 10%, and the redirect now names a different company.
Before resuming I need the new legal entity, its licence and the updated disclosure in writing.
Thanks for flagging. The advertiser changed processing partners. I will send the documents.

steps.say: Pause first, then tell the network in writing. Read the chat. The buyer says they paused the Kenya loan offer today, because the live fee is fifteen percent where their file shows ten, and the redirect now names a different company. Then they say what they need before resuming: the new legal entity, its licence, and the updated disclosure, in writing. The manager explains the advertiser changed partners and will send documents. Factual, specific, with dates and screenshots.

steps.h: Complaint signals to watch
steps.p: Complaints rarely arrive as a letter from a regulator. They show up first in places you already have access to. Check each one in your monthly routine.
d: Ad comments and hides|Words like scam, hidden fee, harassment
App reviews|New patterns in low-star reviews
Network notes|Returns for 'never applied'
Your inbox|Users asking who you are
steps.say: Complaints rarely arrive as a letter from a regulator. They show up first in places you already have access to. Look at the cards. Ad comments and hides, with words like scam, hidden fee or harassment. App reviews, with new patterns in low-star reviews. Network notes, like returns for never applied. And your inbox, with users asking who you are. Check each one in your monthly routine.

steps.h: When and where to report
steps.p: Pausing protects your campaign. Reporting can protect other people. If you find a lender acting illegally or harming borrowers, consider telling the bodies that can act. Names below are examples to confirm.

Most have online complaint forms. Keep your report factual: what you saw, when, with screenshots. steps.h: Common monitoring mistakes
steps.p: Most buyers check at launch. Problems come from what happens after, when attention is on scaling and creatives and nobody is looking at the partner.

a.title: Mistake

b.title: Fix
items: Resume only with documents in writing

Trusting the offer link never changes, so walk the funnel each month. Ignoring comments on ads, so read them weekly. And resuming on a verbal promise, so resume only with documents in writing.

steps.h: Act on harm before profit
steps.p: When you see signs of harm, pause first and investigate second. The order matters to users, platforms and regulators, and it is the order you can defend later.

d.text: If you learn a partner is unlicensed, shaming borrowers or hiding fees, pause immediately and tell the network in writing. Consider reporting to the regulator. Never keep running while you wait for an answer.
